To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. descriptor_candidate.name: length_to_included_sphere_confinement_ratio
descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: For adsorbate-framework pairs at fixed framework included-sphere size lsd_p, molecules with a larger heavy-atom maximum pair distance (GeDi, a long-axis/size proxy) confined within a smaller included sphere along the free path (lsd_p, a cavity-size proxy along the diffusion path) experience greater rotational hindrance and therefore a larger entropy loss (Sgas-Sads)/R. Equivalently, at fixed GeDi, a smaller lsd_p increases the predicted entropy loss, consistent with the reported FER-vs-FAU and MFI-vs-FAU rotational entropy loss comparisons.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: The evidence reports that rotational entropy loss grows with confinement (smaller cavities, MFI vs FAU; FER vs FAU), but D0 provides no global cavity diameter Di. lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path and is used here as an explicit, non-identical proxy for cavity size along the diffusion pathway; it is NOT bottleneck Df and NOT necessarily the global cavity Di cited in the sources. GeDi, the largest distance between two molecular atoms in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, proxies the molecular long dimension that must reorient inside the confined space; it is not a full all-atom rotational free-volume measure. The ratio is a dimensionless confinement index combining these two imperfect proxies; the mechanism (rotational hindrance scaling with molecule-to-cavity size mismatch) is plausible and source-motivated but unverified in this benchmark, and no source-specific percentage is imported.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The descriptor is disfavored if, holding lsd_p fixed, conditional entropy loss does not increase with GeDi over the training quantile range, or if holding GeDi fixed the loss does not decrease with lsd_p. A competing explanation that would falsify the rotational mechanism is that the observed association is driven instead by translational confinement better proxied by Vol or by bottleneck passage (lsd_f) rather than included-sphere size (lsd_p); if q_Vol/q_lsd_f or q_Vol alone explains the same variation while q_GeDi/q_lsd_p adds nothing, this descriptor is redundant.

This transfers the reported FER/FAU cavity-confinement/rotational-entropy relation (E02, C2) and the MFI/FAU comparison (E01, E04) only conditionally, via lsd_f as a bottleneck proxy, not as an equality with the reported average cavity diameter.
final_candidate.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement reduces configurational freedom of translation and rotation (E03, C3). The descriptor couples the framework passing-bottleneck proxy lsd_f (Zeo++ Df, explicitly NOT global cavity diameter Di) with the adsorbate largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi in the implicit-H representation. It is dimensionless, finite, and strictly decreasing in GeDi at fixed lsd_f. Proxy limitations: lsd_f measures the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path, not the cavity where rotational loss was reported, so the mapping from Di to Df is an unverified assumption; GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance, not a full van der Waals extent, and single-site molecules legitimately have GeDi = 0 (descriptor equals 1, the maximally open limit within this proxy); AV is not used, so no mass-specific free-volume claim is made. The descriptor re-expresses information already in D0; it is proposed as one falsifiable candidate, not as an established relation.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: If, holding lsd_f fixed at training values (e.g., the training median 5.16326 angstrom), the conditional prediction of entropy loss over R does not increase with GeDi over its training support (0 to 10.97181443 angstrom), the confinement-extent mechanism is not supported by this benchmark. final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (i) the free-path bottleneck Df is a usable proxy for confinement relevant to rotational and translational entropy loss, which is NOT the average cavity diameter Di cited in E02; (ii) the heavy-atom pair distance GeDi proxies the adsorbate extent that must fit through or rotate within the confining geometry, in the implicit-H representation; (iii) the reported FER/FAU and MFI/FAU entropy-loss contrasts transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks and regime. review_issues.explanation: Proxy-role mismatch: the hypothesis (E02, C2) is framed around the reported AVERAGE CAVITY diameter Di as the confinement descriptor, but the draft uses lsd_f, the Zeo++ Df largest free sphere that can PASS THROUGH a periodic path. These are different geometric quantities. For cage-window topologies (large cages connected by narrow windows), Df reflects the window, not the cage where rotational confinement was reported; Df can therefore rank frameworks oppositely to the cavity diameter cited in the source. The Di-to-Df mapping is asserted, not justified, and remains an unverified assumption.

Mechanism conflation of permeation with confinement: the hypothesis states that GeDi approaching the bottleneck dimension implies fewer accessible configurations, but fitting THROUGH a window governs permeation, while rotational/translational configurational loss was reported for residence INSIDE cages. A molecule larger than the bottleneck relative to the window may nonetheless sit in a large cavity with abundant configurational freedom. The link 'small ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f+GeDi) implies large entropy loss' is a plausible-sounding but unverified physical inference, not supported by the cited evidence as stated.

GeDi is the largest HEAVY-ATOM-CENTER pair distance in the implicit-H representation, not the van der Waals extent of the molecule. Whether a molecule fits through or rotates within a pore depends on the vdW envelope (including hydrogens and probe radii), not on nucleus-center distances. Using GeDi as the 'molecular extent that must fit' is a proxy choice with unquantified error, especially for hydrogen-rich adsorbates; it is not full all-atom molecular geometry, as the input record itself states.

Representational zero mapped to a physical claim: 54 training rows (single-site rotor case) have the legitimate GeDi = 0, which maps the descriptor to exactly 1, described as the 'maximally open limit'. This is a convention of the implicit-H representation, not a verified statement that single-site species experience no extent-based confinement; the physical interpretation of descriptor value 1 for these rows is untested. The draft correctly refuses imputation, but the boundary semantics should not be read as validated physics.

The cited evidence (E01-E04) reports specific framework-pair contrasts (MFI vs FAU, FER vs FAU) with unresolved temperature, loading, and framework chemistry; the quoted percentages (3-fold, 38% vs 20%) are source-specific and explicitly must not become universal constants. No cited source derives or motivates the specific functional form lsd_f/(lsd_f + GeDi); the monotone decreasing saturating form is an empirical choice. Also, the additive denominator mixes a framework length and an adsorbate length with no independent physical meaning as a sum.

Related literature (E05, C5) reports that treating guests as immobile under the RRHO approximation overestimates entropy losses and that retained adsorbate mobility must be accounted for; E07 derives adsorption entropy via partition functions only for rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom. The draft's configurational-freedom narrative does not distinguish mobility regimes or rotor cases, and no evidence item establishes a quantitative molecule-extent-to-entropy-loss mapping in this benchmark's regime. Support is motivational and conditional only.

The knowledge graph grants only conditional MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS edges (e.g., cavity_rotation to lsd_f, GeDi under C2); absence of stronger graph support is unknown, not disproof. The execution check confirms structural executability and monotone behavior only; semantics, causality, and novelty of the combination remain unverified and are honestly labeled as such in the draft. No target values are provided, so the predicted loss direction cannot be checked against data.

To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. descriptor_candidate.name: window_to_cage_contrast
descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: for a fixed largest included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, proxy for the largest local free space along the periodic diffusion path), a larger passing bottleneck Df relative to that included sphere indicates a more uniformly open, channel-like pore architecture rather than a cage-window architecture. Transferring the reported confinement-entropy relation (E02, C2) and the MFI/FAU comparison (E01, E04) only conditionally, greater uniform openness at fixed local free space reduces confinement of adsorbate translational motion (E03: both translational and rotational motions contribute to entropy loss), so the entropy loss over R is predicted to decrease as lsd_f/(lsd_f+lsd_p) increases. This descriptor contrasts two distinct framework diameter roles (Df vs Dif) rather than mixing framework and adsorbate geometry as in the previously appended descriptor lsd_f/(lsd_f+GeDi).
descriptor_candidate.rationale: lsd_f (Zeo++ Df) is the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path (bottleneck), and lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere along that free path; neither equals a global cavity diameter Di. Their contrast is used purely as a structural proxy distinguishing narrow-window vs uniformly-open connectivity. A low ratio (small Df at fixed Dif) signals cage-window architecture where accessible positions are separated by narrow constrictions, which is hypothesized to increase translational configurational restriction. This is an empirical proxy hypothesis, not an established mechanism; the mapping from bottleneck geometry to entropy loss is unverified in this benchmark.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_p fixed, entropy loss over R shows no monotonic decrease with increasing lsd_f/(lsd_f+lsd_p), or if the observed relation is fully explained by lsd_f alone (i.e., the Dif contrast adds no conditional information beyond the bottleneck diameter, making the ratio redundant with bottleneck-only proxies). A competing explanation is that entropy loss tracks the absolute bottleneck size regardless of the included-along-path sphere, in which case the descriptor reduces to a reparameterized lsd_f.

appended.name: bottleneck_to_adsorbate_extent_ratio
appended.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: for a fixed framework free-sphere bottleneck Df, an adsorbate whose largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi approaches the bottleneck dimension has fewer accessible configurations, so a larger fraction of its gas-phase rotational and translational entropy is lost on adsorption; as the ratio lsd_f/(lsd_f+GeDi) increases (more open bottleneck relative to molecular extent), the entropy loss over R is predicted to decrease. This transfers the reported FER/FAU cavity-confinement/rotational-entropy relation (E02, C2) and the MFI/FAU comparison (E01, E04) only conditionally, via lsd_f as a bottleneck proxy, not as an equality with the reported average cavity diameter.
appended.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement reduces configurational freedom of translation and rotation (E03, C3). The descriptor couples the framework passing-bottleneck proxy lsd_f (Zeo++ Df, explicitly NOT global cavity diameter Di) with the adsorbate largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi in the implicit-H representation. It is dimensionless, finite, and strictly decreasing in GeDi at fixed lsd_f. Proxy limitations: lsd_f measures the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path, not the cavity where rotational loss was reported, so the mapping from Di to Df is an unverified assumption; GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance, not a full van der Waals extent, and single-site molecules legitimately have GeDi = 0 (descriptor equals 1, the maximally open limit within this proxy); AV is not used, so no mass-specific free-volume claim is made. The descriptor re-expresses information already in D0; it is proposed as one falsifiable candidate, not as an established relation.
appended.falsification_criteria: If, holding lsd_f fixed at training values (e.g., the training median 5.16326 angstrom), the conditional prediction of entropy loss over R does not increase with GeDi over its training support (0 to 10.97181443 angstrom), the confinement-extent mechanism is not supported by this benchmark. Competing explanation: the apparent association could be driven by adsorbate size correlating with energetic (enthalpic) rather than entropic confinement effects, or by lsd_f acting mainly as a general openness proxy independent of adsorbate extent; if substituting a random adsorbate-independent function of lsd_f alone performs equivalently, the coupling term adds no support.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (i) the free-path bottleneck Df is a usable proxy for confinement relevant to rotational and translational entropy loss, which is NOT the average cavity diameter Di cited in E02; (ii) the heavy-atom pair distance GeDi proxies the adsorbate extent that must fit through or rotate within the confining geometry, in the implicit-H representation; (iii) the reported FER/FAU and MFI/FAU entropy-loss contrasts transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks and regime. These are proxy assumptions and empirical choices, not established causality.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] is strictly positive, so the denominator never vanishes and no division-by-zero occurs. GeDi = 0 for single-site molecules is a legitimate physical zero of the implicit-H representation and is preserved: it maps to the descriptor value 1 (maximally open relative to extent), not to an imputed median. The descriptor is bounded in (0, 1] on training data and remains finite for all positive lsd_f and non-negative GeDi.
